- superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work
- superpowers:receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
- superpowers:requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
- superpowers:subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- superpowers:systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- superpowers:test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
- superpowers:using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
- superpowers:using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
- superpowers:verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- superpowers:writing-plans: Use when you have a spec or requirements for a multi-step task, before touching code
- superpowers:writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus broken CLAUDE.md rules and cleanups where the model's recipe covers them; see /simplify) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. - Use the max level only when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask for it, never on your own judgment: it is the costliest level and starts many reviewer subagents.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read FIRST, before you answer, run a command or open a file (already started? read it now); don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file; if nothing hits, load this skill).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a theme, a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:built-in-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:chrome-browser: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.
- anthropic-skills:computer-use: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.
- anthropic-skills:deep-research: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (editable docs people share and comment on; the default for any document, named as a doc or not: a document, report, proposal, resume, cover letter, letter, contract, policy, form, template, worksheet, essay, handbook, guide, how-to, cheat sheet, SOP or other writing to keep, share, collaborate on, send, submit, print or sign; a doc exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs, so needing a file to send, attach, upload, submit or print is no reason to pick Word, and a file nobody asked for is a doc, not Word; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat; a pasted claude.ai artifact link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; Word or another file format named, tracked changes wanted, or a .docx to change or use as a template → that format's skill): making one → if no docs-connector instructions are in context, call its `guide` (topic.instructions) first; then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:setup-writing-style: Learns how the user writes from their own sent messages and docs, and builds a voice profile so future drafts sound like them instead of generic AI. The profile is saved as the my-writing-style skill. Use when the user asks to set up, learn, or capture their writing voice, or complains that drafts sound generic or unlike them and no my-writing-style profile exists. Only for drafting text the user will send as themselves, not for Claude's own replies.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

  `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<branch>` == `git rev-parse HEAD`.
* **User order restated 2026-11-18 (permanent, every account):** at the START of every session restore and verify the
  five-minute GitHub autosave (`python3 -I scripts/autosave-status.py` → `AUTOSAVE OK … (match)`), save immediately after
  every kept visual improvement and before ending, verify remote SHA == local HEAD. Since 2026-11-18 every autosave also
  snapshots each specialist worktree's UNFINISHED edits (read-only) into `backups/wip/<branch>/` (`tracked.patch`, small new
  files, `INFO.json` with restore steps; since 2026-11-19 ~23:55 UTC files up to 5 MB / 150 MB per worktree, so full-size

# The user's detailed visual requirements for every approved Rainbow screen (round 26, 2026-11-20 ~13:00 UTC, verbatim)

Binding for EVERY specialist and every screen, together with `docs/briefs/2026-11-18-r13/USER_VISUAL_GOAL_R13.md`. The user's own words follow.

---

CLAUDIA — MY DETAILED VISUAL REQUIREMENTS FOR EVERY APPROVED RAINBOW SCREEN

Please use this message as my continuing visual brief for the entire game and share the relevant requirements with every specialist.

My goal is for someone playing my mobile game to recognise the world shown in my original approved screens immediately—and to keep seeing that same world as Benny swims forward, steers, passes the scenery and moves into the next stage.

I want the closest possible match to my approved screens. Ideally, the appearance would match exactly. My acceptable visual target is approximately 90–95% likeness, with 95% preferred. Treat that as my visual acceptance standard. Explain and show the remaining differences rather than giving me percentages that have not been established.

The result must be a real, responsive mobile game. Benny's movement, the scenery, the water, the camera, the collectibles and the transitions must work together during actual play.

## 1. Use each screen's own original approved image as its visual specification

For every screen, inspect the original approved reference already saved in the project. Use it to establish:

- The overall composition and the distinctive shape of the scene.
- The river's width, curves, height changes and position within the environment.
- The cyan water, pink or magenta edges, highlights and reflections.
- The shape, size, density and placement of foam and floating bubbles.
- The tunnel, rings, walls, openings, machinery and other scenery.
- The colours, lighting, shadows, metallic surfaces and sense of depth.
- Benny's appearance, proportions and relationship to the water.
- The size and arrangement of coins, arrows and other visible gameplay elements.
- The HUD's layout, proportions, typography and styling.

Preserve each screen's individual identity. Screen 04's gold tunnel, Screen 06's curling crest, Screen 07's winding river and Screen 08's final chamber should each remain recognisable.

My latest specific corrections take precedence where I have explicitly requested a change. For example, my request for cleaner, lower pink edges on Screen 04 should guide that correction while the rest of its approved design is preserved.

## 2. Maintain the approved appearance throughout movement

The opening frame is only one part of the requirement.

The approved visual quality must continue through the entrance, early movement, middle, late section, ending, left steering, right steering and transition into the next screen.

I expect perspective to change naturally as Benny moves. Nearby objects should pass the camera, distant objects should approach, and scenery should become visible from new angles. Throughout that movement, the world must retain the approved design, materials, colours, proportions and quality.

When movement reveals a surface or area that the original picture did not show, make it a convincing continuation of that same approved environment.

Please inspect what happens when Benny:

- Approaches and passes a gold ring.
- Travels alongside a wall or foam bank.
- Moves around a bend.
- Steers strongly toward either side.
- Swims over a crest or down a drop.
- Reaches the end of the stage.
- Enters the next environment.

Those moving views are part of the design requirement. They need the same care as the opening view.

## 3. Make the water clean, detailed and consistent with each reference

The water is one of the most important parts of this game. It occupies much of the screen and needs to remain attractive while moving.

Match each approved screen's water in colour, shape, gloss, depth and detail:

- Preserve the bright cyan and blue body of the river, with the appropriate pink or magenta edges.
- Match the approved balance of blue, pink, white highlights and reflected colour.
- Keep highlights shaped and sized appropriately. Large white sheets, excessively long glints and sharp spikes should not overwhelm the water.
- Give the water coherent curves, ripples and flowing detail that follow the river.
- Keep the surface visually continuous around Benny and between sections of the channel.
- Resolve visible seams, speckled joins, stretched textures, cut-out edges, abrupt colour changes and patches that look detached from the surrounding water.
- Keep the pink edges fluid and glossy, with the height and thickness appropriate to that screen.
- Make reflections and highlights belong to the water's surface and movement.

Match the foam to the original reference too. Where it forms soft banks, it should have rounded, varied shapes and believable spacing. Where the reference shows individual bubbles, preserve that distinction. Avoid making every screen use the same foam treatment.

Benny's contact with the water should feel natural. Ripples, splashes and his wake should join the surrounding surface cleanly and respond to his movement.

## 4. Keep the scenery detailed and the camera useful during play

The background and surrounding scenery matter just as much as Benny.

As he passes through the environment:

- Gold rings should retain their approved shape, spacing, metallic appearance and lighting.
- Perforated washer walls should retain clear, properly shaped details as they approach the camera.
- Curved surfaces should remain visually coherent through turns and changes in perspective.
- The scene should preserve its approved sense of scale and depth.
- Lighting and colour should remain consistent across neighbouring surfaces and stage connections.

The camera should follow Benny naturally and keep the upcoming route understandable. Steering should allow me to see where he is going while preserving the intended feeling of swimming through the washer.

Please correct any view where a nearby wall or oversized foreground surface takes over so much of the screen that the approved river and scenery disappear.

## 5. Keep Benny consistent with his approved appearance

Use the approved Benny throughout the game:

- The same fluffy pink body, silhouette and proportions.
- The same purple-and-cream knitted hat, with the correct stripe pattern, width and texture.
- The same pom-pom and yellow star, with the correct shape, scale and placement.
- The same soft, detailed fur and overall character quality.

His hat should retain its knitted appearance, and his body should retain its soft, fluffy appearance at normal phone viewing size.

Keep him at the correct waterline and scale for the camera. His swimming, leaning and turning should feel connected to the river. His wake and splashes should follow his movement.

Allow natural perspective changes and animation while preserving his identity. The character should look consistent when centred, steering left, steering right, approaching the camera or moving farther away.

## 6. Individual requirements for the screens we are reviewing

### Screen 04 — THROUGH THE FIVE ARROWS

Preserve the approved gold-ring tunnel, blue river, pink accents, foam, bubbles, coins and five-arrow sequence.

My specific requirements are:

- Keep the blue water clear, bright and detailed.
- Keep the pink edges lower, cleaner and neatly contained so the gold structure remains visible.
- Preserve the gold rings' shape, depth and attractive metallic lighting as Benny moves through them.
- Keep the foam soft and appropriately sized along the river. The distant foam should form the intended banks instead of looking like unrelated bubbles.
- Refine the long glints near the camera so they suit the approved water.
- Keep exactly five arrows arranged neatly, with the intended direction, spacing and appearance.
- Make Benny's normal route carry him naturally through that sequence.
- Keep arrows, coins, water and scenery aligned during movement, with no clipping or sudden positional jumps.

Use the three additional Screen 04 artwork views I already approved where appropriate. Judge their appearance in the playable scene as Benny advances.

### Screen 05 — FLOW INTO THE CURRENT

Preserve the long winding river through the purple-and-gold washer tunnel.

My specific requirements are:

- Keep the broad cyan river and magenta edges following the approved sweeping course.
- Make the channel boundaries, foam and coin trail belong to the same curves.
- Preserve the crisp perforations in the purple walls and the gold ring structure.
- Keep the bright, glossy water detailed as the camera moves forward.
- Maintain the approved balance between river, tunnel and distant scenery.
- Give the end of the stage and the hard-left view particular attention, because those remain open items.
- Check the right-steering view as well so a correction on one side does not create a new problem on the other.

The whole stage should feel like travelling through the winding environment shown in the approved image.

### Screen 06 — CREST THE RINSE ARCH

The curling water crest and curved approach to the off-centre tunnel are defining features of this approved screen.

My specific requirements are:

- Preserve the crest's recognisable shape and its relationship to the tunnel.
- Continue the river's intended curves as Benny progresses.
- Keep the coin trail and foam following that same course.
- Frame the tunnel and crest in a way that preserves the approved composition while allowing natural forward movement.
- Correct the opening blue cone beneath Benny. His contact with the water should show the shallow ripple and integrated wake appropriate to the reference.
- Remove any visible edge or water mismatch left by the area where the painted Benny was removed.
- Keep the foam at an appropriate height so the water and scenery remain visible.
- Maintain the river's shape and detail beyond the opening, through the middle and end.

Please deliver the opening comparison I am still owed: the original approved image, the version I previously saw and the corrected candidate.

### Screen 07 — DIVE THE WASHER TUBE

Preserve the approved long, winding river extending through the purple-and-gold ring tube.

My specific requirements are:

- Make the entire visible river follow broad S-shaped bends.
- Curve the cyan water, pink edges, both foam banks and coin trail together.
- Align Benny's route, steering limits and collisions with that same channel.
- Preserve the feeling of a substantial winding river throughout the middle and end.
- Keep the upcoming route visible while steering, particularly in the section where the purple wall previously dominated the view.
- Preserve the fuller foam candidate while refining its shape, size and spacing to suit the approved reference.
- Keep the ending and drop consistent with the approved river's appearance.
- Make the water and foam connect smoothly into the latest Screen 08 candidate, K23-3.
- Correct the speckled band and abrupt change in water appearance around that connection.

After the corrections, show the same complete labelled sequence covering the entrance, both steering directions, ending and transition into Screen 08.

### Screen 08 — FINAL SPIN CHAMBER

Preserve the approved final chamber, gold architecture, purple walls, distant washer window, purple towel on its ledge and winding river leading toward them.

My specific requirements are:

- Retain the river's recognisable S-shaped course and foam boundaries as Benny advances.
- Keep its width and foreground shape consistent with the approved environment.
- Preserve detailed, glossy water without allowing a broad bright sheet to obscure the intended river.
- Refine the sharp, spiky glints while keeping the approved sparkle and lighting.
- Match the coins' apparent size and placement to the reference as closely as the moving perspective allows.
- Resolve the towel's doubled or ghosted appearance while preserving its intended lighting and depth.
- Keep the window, ledge, towel and chamber architecture coherent throughout forward movement and steering.
- Preserve the completed K23-3 work and improve from that saved candidate.

K23-3 remains a candidate awaiting my visual approval.

### Every other approved screen

Apply these same requirements to all remaining approved screens, using each one's own original reference and my existing decisions.

Identify that screen's distinctive scenery, water, character placement, lighting and gameplay elements. Maintain those characteristics throughout its sequence.

## 7. Make the whole experience feel like one polished mobile game

Check how the screens connect, as well as how they look individually.

Water, river direction, scenery depth, lighting, Benny's position and his movement should connect convincingly across stage boundaries. Correct gaps, abrupt resets, mismatched surfaces and disconnected landings.

Preserve working controls, collectibles, collisions, pause and progression while making the visual improvements.

Keep the HUD clean and consistent with the approved design, with readable text, properly aligned icons and live game values.

The final combined result needs to work on an Android phone with responsive controls and stable gameplay. Clearly identify whether a demonstration shows an individual candidate, a combined preview or the current Android build.

## 8. Show me clear evidence of improvement

For each meaningful change, provide:

- The ORIGINAL APPROVED reference.
- The BEFORE version.
- The NEW candidate.
- Separate, full-size images with clear labels.
- A continuous gameplay clip showing the relevant movement.

Capture BEFORE and NEW under comparable conditions: the same stage position, camera settings, steering sequence and playback speed.

Include the start, middle, end and strong left/right steering where relevant. Include the complete transition when a change affects the next screen.

Show normal-speed gameplay first. A labelled half-speed version can help me inspect details, but the appearance must also hold up at normal speed.

For each result, tell me:

- What specifically became closer to the approved reference.
- What still looks different.
- Whether the change introduced any new visual or gameplay problem.
- What remains to be corrected next.

At viewpoints that correspond to the approved image, compare the composition closely. For deeper and turning views, assess whether they preserve the same world, materials, shapes, colours and quality.

My final approval comes from seeing those results. Keep successful work saved and continue the other authorized tasks while individual candidates await my verdict.

## 9. Continue toward this result

Please assess the latest playable versions against these requirements and give me an honest answer about which parts are improving and which still need work.

Continue from the existing saved project and successful changes. Keep the current specialists working within the authorizations already given, and make sure each specialist understands the requirements for their screen.

My goal is a clean, attractive, professional mobile game where the approved artwork feels brought to life—throughout the entire experience of Benny swimming through it.
